- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) or volatile, model overreacts downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots downward — reduce forecast slope to prevent overcorrection.  
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in early forecast periods — if true outcome deviates from recent 7-day average by >3%, adjust forecast toward that average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates late-period volatility — increase forecast tail risk (last 5–7 days) by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or mixed.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.3 → +0.3), model fails to anticipate — add a 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast in next 3–5 days.
